body.statement: There exist constants \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\pi>0\) and a nonempty compact interval \(H_0\subseteq[0,\bar H]\) such that, uniformly for \(h\in H_0\), with probability at least \(\pi+o(1)\) the bounded-Lipschitz distance between the conditional ordinary Efron-bootstrap law of the centered, \(n^{1/4}\)-scaled endpoint pair and its sampling law exceeds \(\varepsilon\). For the exact \(B_n\)-candidate retained algorithm in the retained-bootstrap definition, the same conclusion holds for \(\widehat{\mathbb L}_n^{\mathrm{ret}}\) because its scaled coordinate marginals converge to the random kernel \(\mathcal K_h(Z)\) and its reflection, while \(\sup_{h\in H_0}P_{n,h}(M_n=0)\to0\). Consequently, percentile intervals formed from the ordinary conditional law or from the left-continuous retained quantiles \(Q_{n,-}^{\mathrm{ret}}\) and \(Q_{n,+}^{\mathrm{ret}}\) fail to attain uniform endpoint coverage; the finite Monte Carlo realization of the feasibility-retained workflow in Watson et al.'s Theorem 4 is not contact-uniform.
body.justification: A random limiting kernel turns a qualitative boundary warning into a falsifiable nonuniformity theorem for a named implementation.
body.gap: Andrews treats a projected boundary estimator and Fang--Santos treat directionally differentiable maps; neither covers the half-Hölder map \(x\mapsto\sqrt{x_+}\) or endogenous retention in leaky-IV bounds.
body.consumer: The result prevents nominal percentile claims from being reported at empirically plausible near-feasibility designs.
